newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An explosion yesterday morning ripped the side out of the seventh floor of the almost-completed President Tower complex resulting in a fire which left three people dead and over 100 injured. Fire and rescue services rapidly responded and a number of helicopters, in daring sorties, plucked more than 93 people from the roof of the building. (BUSINESS DAY) ((BANGKOK POST)

- Constitution draftsmen will today consider the final "framework" for mapping out the new charter, dealing with controversial issues such as requiring Cabinet members to resign their parliamentary seats and the indirect election of senators. Spokesman for the drafting committee of the Constitution Drafting Assembly says the panel will also consider proposals to ensure the prime minister completes a four-year term after a general election. (THE NATION)

- The number of HIV-infected pregnant women in the northern provinces is increasing, particularly in Chiang Mai, health officials say. Pregnant women comprise 5.4 percent of all HIV-infected people in the province and the figure is likely to increase. (THE NATION) + + + +

- ASEAN finance ministers will agree to work on broader cooperation in banking and finance, financial and capital markets, customs procedures, insurance business, taxation and public finance when they meet for the first time in Phuket this weekend. Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan will chair the ground-breaking event that will bring all the finance ministers from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations together to lay out cooperation in the sensitive financial sector. (THE NATION)

- Thailand is working hard to ensure that Krirk-krai Jirapaet, Thai Ambassador to the World Trade Organisation, will be nominated as chairman of the working group to examine the relationship between trade and investment. But some members want the chairmen of three working groups to be appointed as a package, as agreed by WTO ministers at their first meeting in Singapore last December. (BANGKOK POST)

- The country's largest finance company, Finance One Plc, will start foreign exchange business in the third quarter of this year. The Bank of Thailand last year granted permission to the company to begin foreign exchange operations. Finance One has not projected revenue from the new business at this juncture. (BUSINESS DAY)
